summary: Iteration 1 achieved a confirmed 54.5× speedup on the npartitions workload (1.28s → 0.023s) by rewriting the inner Kloosterman sum function with four synergistic optimizations: O(log k) memoized Dedekind sums, Kloosterman symmetry to halve iterations, a hardware-float fast path for low-precision iterations, and gmpy2 MPFR cosine for high-precision iterations. All correctness tests pass.
key_points: Prediction of >10× speedup was confirmed with 54.5× actual (mean 1.2774s → 0.0234s, std 0.0034s). The dominant contributor was replacing the O(j²) inline Dedekind sum with an O(j log j) cached reciprocity formula, which alone likely accounts for ~30× of the improvement.

Correctness is fully preserved: all covering tests in test_partitions.py pass (1/1), and exact integer results verified for n=0–5, 25, 100, 200, 1000, 2000, 10000, 100000. Early termination of the HRR outer loop was explicitly tested and rejected — it silently corrupts results by ±1 to ±9.

Remaining optimization headroom is small: the 0.023s runtime is dominated by the outer HRR loop structure and _d (sinh) computations (~10% of original time). Potential next steps include precomputed coprime lists (saving ~0.002s), _d optimization at low precision, and ablation to quantify each component's contribution — but diminishing returns suggest this campaign could be concluded.
